# tfutils_http_ready_wait (Resource)

On create, waits until a GET request to `url` returns status 200, for example until a DNS record and a load balancer route a new endpoint. Apply fails with the last status or error when the create timeout passes. Read makes no request, so plans do not depend on the endpoint; the wait runs again only when `url` or `triggers` change. Destroy does nothing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tfutils_http_ready_wait" "argocd" {
  url = "https://argocd.example.com/healthz"

  triggers = {
    ingress_uid = kubectl_manifest.ingress.uid
  }

  timeouts {
    create = "20m"
  }

  depends_on = [helm_release.argocd]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `url` (String) URL to request.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values whose change replaces the resource and runs the wait again.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `url`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
